title: SOTA Generative Media Panel — Dumitru Erhan, Shane Gu & Nicole Brichtova, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: A Google DeepMind panel on generative media (Nano Banana, Gemini Omni) covering model specialization vs unification, language as an intermediate representation, and how they evaluate outputs.

takeaways.technique: Human side-by-side evals for close calls
takeaways.what_they_do: When two model checkpoints are close, they make decisions by having ~10 people look at outputs side by side in a room rather than relying on automated metrics.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we literally make decisions based on like looking at outputs side by side. Sometimes like in a room like I've been in rooms where there's like 10 of us

takeaways.what_they_do: They separate objectively checkable properties (e.g. OCR text rendering correctness) from subjective aesthetics, automating the former and reserving humans for the latter.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there are some things that are a little bit more objective ... you can kind of OCR things out ... those things are like a little bit more auto ratable

takeaways.what_they_do: They rely on expert users who use the models in real workflows to catch systematic artifacts (e.g. wedding rings on every hand) that internal teams miss.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our model tends to put rings wedding rings on on on hand ... we would not have noticed necessarily while while developing this

takeaways.technique: Specialized small model for fast iteration
takeaways.what_they_do: They ship a cheaper/faster model (Nano Banana 2 light) that is close to frontier quality for most use cases, reserving the big model for hard cases.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our fastest, cheapest um image model ... it gets really close to the frontier quality of of the kind of mainland bigger models

takeaways.what_they_do: They note that combining strong understanding models agentically beats trying to do everything in one pass, even while unified models trend upward.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's like a lot you can do if you uh basically take like really good video understanding image understanding Gemini agentically

takeaways.technique: Rich intermediate representation over terse captions
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue that if the conditioning representation is too sparse, generation becomes too stochastic; richer conditioning reduces ambiguity.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you basically don't have enough uh representation that basically means the condition on the language the generation is very multimodal
